milkDrinks.title: Milk drinks and latte art
milkDrinks.intro: Proportions are default estimates, not an SCA standard. Adjust them to your taste.
milkDrinks.milkTemperatureNote: Range to be checked against a primary source (NM-06). It is not an SCA standard.

espresso.name: Espresso
espresso.description: The base of every drink. No milk.
espresso.step1: Prepare the coffee dose and pull the shot.
espresso.step2: Serve at once, in a warmed cup.
espresso.tip: Espresso has no foam. The foam tip applies to drinks with milk.

cappuccino.name: Cappuccino
cappuccino.description: Three equal parts: espresso, milk and foam.
cappuccino.step1: Pour the espresso into a warmed cup.
cappuccino.step2: Aerate the milk briefly, with the wand just below the surface, until the volume rises slightly.
cappuccino.step3: Move the wand deeper and heat the milk within the temperature range, swirling the pitcher.
cappuccino.step4: Tap the pitcher on the counter and swirl to break up large bubbles.
cappuccino.step5: Pour the milk into the cup and spoon the foam on top.
cappuccino.tip: Foam should be smooth and glossy, like wet paint. If it collapses quickly, the milk may have been too hot.

latte.name: Latte
latte.description: More milk than a cappuccino, with a thin layer of foam.
latte.step1: Pour the espresso into the cup.
latte.step2: Aerate the milk briefly, until a thin foam forms.
latte.step3: Heat the milk within the temperature range, rolling the pitcher so the foam blends into the milk.
latte.step4: Tap the pitcher and swirl until glossy.
latte.step5: Pour the milk slowly, starting in the middle of the cup, with the pitcher low over the surface.
latte.tip: Latte art depends on how smooth the foam is, not on how hard you pour. Start in the middle and narrow the stream at the end.

flatWhite.name: Flat white
flatWhite.description: Espresso and milk with microfoam, without a thick layer.
flatWhite.step1: Pour the espresso into the cup.
flatWhite.step2: Aerate the milk very briefly, only until microfoam forms.
flatWhite.step3: Heat the milk within the temperature range, swirling the pitcher.
flatWhite.step4: Swirl the milk so the foam is even, without large bubbles.
flatWhite.step5: Pour the milk from the pitcher through the microfoam so a white dot remains on the surface.
flatWhite.tip: Microfoam should be even and glossy, with no layer of foam on top. Thick foam means you aerated for too long.

mocha.name: Mocha
mocha.description: Espresso with chocolate syrup and milk.
mocha.step1: Pour the chocolate syrup into the bottom of the cup.
mocha.step2: Add the espresso and stir well so the syrup dissolves.
mocha.step3: Aerate the milk briefly, then heat it within the temperature range.
mocha.step4: Tap the pitcher and swirl until glossy.
mocha.step5: Pour the milk into the cup and spoon a thin layer of foam on top.
mocha.tip: Pour the syrup first so it does not settle at the bottom. Foam on a mocha should be thin and smooth.

dialin.bitterDesc: Ashy, astringent, harsh, lingering dry bitterness. Heavy tannins over-extracted.
dialin.bitterRemedy: Remedy: Grind coarser, lower water temperature (-2°C), reduce contact time, or minimize agitation.
dialin.balancedDesc: Clear natural sweetness, vibrant acidity, complex floral/fruity notes, clean finish.
dialin.ratioSubtitle: Bidirectional calculation: dose to water or target water to required bean dose.
